SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. I. D. REGISTRY Foreign Section Station, No. I. O. D. 773 Date May 23 1930. 24 - 5 - 30.）

Subject (in full) V. E. Sonder alias John Kosloff.

Made by D. S. Maklaevsky. Forwarded by Thos Robertson Supt. C.

With reference to the attached file, nothing further has been heard of Sonder since he left Shanghai for Vladivostok. Before leaving Shanghai, he informed D.D. Gilerson attached to Central Station that he hoped to receive employment on one of the Moller boats when he arrived at Vladivostok. At that time it was not known that he intended to leave as a Stowaway. Rover states he does not now know of Sonder's whereabouts.

（批：Who 23 5 30）

B. Maklaevsky.
D. S.

D. C.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 10. D 1293
Foreign Section. Station,
REPORT
Date April 24, 1930.
Subject (in full) V.F. Sonder alias John Kozloff.
Made by D.S. Maklaevsky. Forwarded by Thos Robertson C.D.
With reference to the attached letter of April 1, 1930
from Mr. N.F. Allman of Messrs Fleming, Franklin & Allman re:
Vladimir Sonder, who called at Mr. Rover's house at 1 p.m.
on April 1, 1930, inquiries show that Vladimir Sonder visited
Mr. Rover at 18 Carter Road with a view to obtaining assistance
to enter Soviet Russia. Mr. Rover informed him that he did not
deal in such matters and referred him to the German Consul,
who is in charge of Soviet affairs here. During the conversation
with Mr. Rover, V. Sonder confessed that he had been sent by
Eugene Pick to spy out the plan of Mr. Rover's house and to
see if it could be possible to 'plant' incriminating documents
in the house. Mr. Rover is a Soviet Agent and local representative
of the Soviet News Agency "Tass."
With reference to Vladimir Sonder, inquiries show that
he is of Lettish origin and a Soviet subject. He was born on
October 8, 1911 in Vladivostok. In 1918 he left with his
parents for Tientsin where he joined the Catholic School and
remained there until 1922. In 1922 he was sent by his father
(his mother having died in 1920) to Shanghai to join the St.
Xavier's College, Nanzing Road. At the same time his father
proceeded to France and since then V. Sonder has not heard of
him. Sonder graduated from the St. Xavier's College in December
1928, and in January 1929 obtained employment as a clerk with
Messrs Raymond Calle, French Architects, 693 Route de Zi Ka
Wei. He remained in that position until July 1929 when he left,
explaining to his employers that he wished to go to America.
He speaks perfect English and French. On September 30, 1929
he was charged under the name of John Kozloff with larceny,
and was sentenced by the Provisional Court to 6 months'

外侨股。第 站，

日期 1930年4月24日。
主题（全称） V.F. Sonder，化名 John Kozloff。
制作人：D.S. Maklaevsky。呈送人：Thos Robertson 刑事调查科。

关于弗莱明、富兰克林与奥尔曼律师事务所（Messrs Fleming, Franklin & Allman）的 N.F. Allman 先生于1930年4月1日来信提及的 Vladimir Sonder 一事，调查显示，Vladimir Sonder 于1930年4月1日下午1点拜访了 Rover 先生位于卡特路18号的住所，旨在寻求协助进入苏维埃俄国。Rover 先生告知他，自己不处理此类事务，并将其引荐给负责此处苏俄事务的德国领事。在与 Rover 先生的谈话中，V. Sonder 承认是受 Eugene Pick 派遣，来侦察 Rover 先生住宅的布局，并查看是否有可能在屋内“栽赃”陷害性文件。Rover 先生是一名苏维埃特工，也是苏维埃新闻社“塔斯社”（Tass）的本地代表。

关于 Vladimir Sonder，调查显示其为拉脱维亚裔，系苏维埃公民。他于1911年10月8日出生于海参崴。1918年，他随父母前往天津，进入天主教学校就读，并在那里停留至1922年。1922年，由其父亲（其母已于1920年去世）送往上海，进入南京路的圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Xavier's College）。与此同时，其父亲前往法国，此后 V. Sonder 便再无其父音讯。Sonder 于1928年12月从圣方济各沙勿略学院毕业，并于1929年1月在法籍建筑师雷蒙德·卡莱公司（Messrs Raymond Calle，地址：霞飞路693号）受聘为职员。他在该职位上工作至1929年7月离职，向雇主解释称希望前往美国。他能说流利的英语和法语。1929年9月30日，他以 John Kozloff 之名被控犯有盗窃罪，并被临时法院判处6个月

Fleming, Franklin & Allman

WILLIAM S. FLEMING
CORNELL S. FRANKLIN
NORWOOD F. ALLMAN

14 30.
CABLE: "ADVOCATE"
P. O. BOX 952
10 D. 1293.

8 YUEN MING YUEN ROAD
SHANGHAI, CHINA.

April 1, 1930.
（印：RECEIVED ... No. 3631 ... Date ... / 4 / 30 ...）

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir:

Our client, Mr. V. Rover, a Soviet citizen, has
just informed us that at one o'clock, p.m., on April 1, 1930,
a man calling himself Vladimir Sander called at his house
and first inquired if Mr. Rover could help him to go to Russia.
Mr. Rover told him that he had nothing to do with such matters
and could not help him.

During the conversation Mr. Rover asked Mr. Sander
why he had called on him about such a matter as the German
Consul is in charge of Russian interests, and why he did not
call at the German Consul for information and assistance. Mr.
Sander informed Mr. Rover that Mr. Pick had sent him to spy out
Mr. Rover's house to see if there was a possibility of planting
some incriminating or compromising matter in Mr. Rover's house.
Mr. Rover quite naturally requested Mr. Sander to leave his
house and refused to have anything to do with him. Mr. Rover
thinks it desirable that you have this information and we agree
therewith. Mr. Rover's address is No. 18 Carter Road.

Yours very truly,

FLEMING, FRANKLIN & ALLMAN,

By N. F. Allman

NFA:SMC

1930年4月1日。
（印：收到 ... 第 3631 号 ... 日期 ... / 4 / 30 ...）

上海警务处处长，
上海。

尊敬的先生：

我们的客户、苏维埃公民 V. Rover 先生刚刚通知我们，1930年4月1日下午1时，一名自称 Vladimir Sander 的男子到访其寓所，首先询问 Rover 先生是否能帮助他前往俄国。Rover 先生告诉他，自己与此类事务无关，无法提供帮助。

谈话期间，Rover 先生询问 Sander 先生，既然德国领事负责俄国利益相关事务，为何就此事找他，而不去德国领事馆寻求信息和帮助。Sander 先生告知 Rover 先生，是 Pick 先生派他来侦察 Rover 先生的住宅，以查看是否有可能是将某些陷害性或令人难堪的材料“栽赃”到 Rover 先生家中。Rover 先生很自然地要求 Sander 先生离开其寓所，并拒绝与其有任何瓜葛。Rover 先生认为宜将此信息告知阁下，我们也赞同此举。Rover 先生的地址是卡特路18号。

此致，

弗莱明、富兰克林与奥尔曼律师事务所，

由 N. F. Allman 签署

NFA:SMC

Oyr client, Mr. V. Rover, & Soviet citizen, has
